nodes.html: Sole trader vs company vs trust
nodes.text: Sole trader vs company vs trust

nodes.html: Sole trader is the simplest but exposes your personal assets and caps your tax planning. A company limits liability but introduces administration and a separate tax rate. A trust offers flexibility and asset protection but has distribution rules and compliance costs. The right structure depends on your income, growth plans, asset exposure, and succession intentions — not a template.
nodes.text: Sole trader is the simplest but exposes your personal assets and caps your tax planning. A company limits liability but introduces administration and a separate tax rate. A trust offers flexibility and asset protection but has distribution rules and compliance costs. The right structure depends on your income, growth plans, asset exposure, and succession intentions — not a template.

nodes.html: Moving from one structure to another (sole trader to company, company to trust) can trigger a CGT event if done naively. Rollover relief exists under specific conditions — the small-business rollover, replacement-asset rollover, and entity restructuring — but the conditions must be met precisely. Our matched firms execute restructures cleanly, preserving CGT concessions where available.

nodes.q: What is the best structure for a new business?
nodes.a: There is no single best structure — it depends on your income, growth, asset exposure, and succession plans. A sole trader is cheapest but exposes personal assets; a company limits liability but adds administration; a trust offers flexibility but has distribution rules. The matched adviser assesses your situation and recommends the right structure — not a generic 'everyone should be a company' answer.
nodes.aText: There is no single best structure — it depends on your income, growth, asset exposure, and succession plans. A sole trader is cheapest but exposes personal assets; a company limits liability but adds administration; a trust offers flexibility but has distribution rules. The matched adviser assesses your situation and recommends the right structure — not a generic 'everyone should be a company' answer.

nodes.q: Can I change my business structure later?
nodes.a: Yes, but a restructure can trigger CGT if not done under a rollover. Small-business CGT concessions and entity rollovers can preserve the position, but the conditions must be met precisely. The matched adviser plans the restructure to preserve concessions and avoid a taxable event.
nodes.aText: Yes, but a restructure can trigger CGT if not done under a rollover. Small-business CGT concessions and entity rollovers can preserve the position, but the conditions must be met precisely. The matched adviser plans the restructure to preserve concessions and avoid a taxable event.

nodes.q: Does a trust protect my assets?
nodes.a: A discretionary trust can offer asset protection because beneficiaries do not own trust assets directly. But protection depends on the deed, your role, and how distributions are made. The matched adviser reviews your deed and structuring to ensure protection is genuine — not a label that fails under scrutiny.
nodes.aText: A discretionary trust can offer asset protection because beneficiaries do not own trust assets directly. But protection depends on the deed, your role, and how distributions are made. nodes.q: How much does structuring advice cost?
nodes.a: A structure review and recommendation is typically $500–$2,000; a full entity establishment with registrations is usually $1,000–$3,000. The matched adviser gives you a clear quote after reviewing your situation — the matching is free.
